# Objects

#### Course: Learn Java Basics

## Objects

To access the logic written inside a class, we need to create an object.

Think of a class as a blueprint that defines the structure and behavior, while objects are the buildings created based on that blueprint.

To create an object of the Main class we defined earlier, we use the following syntax:

```java
Main obj = new Main();
```

![Syntax to Create an Object](data:image/png;base64,)

Here,

1. The keyword new creates a new object of the Main class.
2. This object is then stored in the variable obj.
3. As shown by the syntax Main obj, the object will have the data type of its class, which is Main in this case.

For now, don't worry about defining your own custom properties inside a class. We will stick to using built-in Java classes to keep our programs simple and focus on learning the basics.
